title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: A program gives the model a goal and three tools, runs whichever tool the model asks for, and stops when the model writes a final answer. Who owns the control flow, meaning who decides which step runs next?

options.text: The program, because the developer fixed the order of steps in advance
The model, because it picks the next step each time round the loop
Both equally, because the program runs every tool the model requests
The tools, because their results decide what happens after each step

items.stem: Booking a slot in your makerspace assistant goes the same way every time: check the calendar, write the booking, send a confirmation. Which design fits this part best?

options.text: An agent, so that the model can pick the sequence afresh for each booking
An agent, because booking needs tools and only agents can call tools
A fixed workflow, because the sequence never changes from one booking to the next
A fixed workflow, because a workflow is always more accurate than an agent

items.stem: A student asks your fixed-workflow assistant to compare two machines, a request none of its paths was built for. What happens?

options.text: It follows only the paths coded in advance, so it needs a new path or a fallback
The model notices the gap and invents a new path for this one request
It turns into an agent for this request, then goes back to being a workflow
It runs every path it has in turn until one of them gives a usable answer

items.stem: A fixed workflow handles each booking in 3 model calls. An agent handles the same booking in 7 model calls on average. If every call costs $0.002, how many dollars more does the agent cost for 500 bookings?
A student's manual question needs one lookup or four, and you cannot tell which from the question. Which design gets the answer right without wasting model calls?

options.text: A fixed workflow that always makes four lookups for every question
A fixed workflow that always makes one lookup for every question
A fixed workflow that always makes two lookups as a middle ground
An agent loop, so that the model decides when it has enough

items.stem: Your code asks the model to label each question "manual" or "booking", then runs a fixed manual path or a fixed booking path. After the label, who picks the next step: the model or the code?
